chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from Dawud ibn Farqad from Bashir al-Nabbal said:

I went out with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) until we reached Ash-Shajara. He said to me, 'O Nabbal.' I replied, 'At your service.' He said, 'Indeed, it is not obligatory upon anyone from the people of this camp to pray four [rak'ahs] each, except me and you, because the time for prayer entered before we set out.'

key_terms.أَرْبَعاً أَرْبَعاً: Four [rak'ahs] each, referring to the shortening of prayers or specific prayer structure

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying four rak'ahs for travelers when prayer time begins before departure?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential principle that the status of a traveler (*musafir*) is determined by the time of departure relative to the prayer window; since the Imam and his companions had not yet left the city limits when the prayer time entered, they were considered residents for that specific prayer. It highlights the nuanced Shia legal distinction between the obligation of *Qasr* (shortened prayer) and *Tamam* (full prayer), noting that the exemption from praying four rak'ahs individually applies specifically to the Imam and the narrator in this unique context, likely due to their specific roles or the precise timing of their exit.
